prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map places the camera wearer’s torso and arms nearest, roughly 0.2–0.7 m away, with the mower directly ahead at about 0.7–1.5 m and the fence, wall, and ground extending behind it by roughly 1–4 m; the mower and wearer are therefore separated by about an arm’s length. Across the five frames, the mower shifts from near the upper-left/centre to the upper-right and back toward the upper-left, while the wearer’s bright torso rotates beneath it, indicating turning and lateral viewpoint changes rather than a clear sustained approach or retreat. Bright arm regions show that the handle remains within the wearer’s reach, while the wearer’s torso occludes much of the lower scene and the mower is partly cut off by the top edge. Depth ordering and broad surface separation are clearer than in RGB, but exact metric distances, thin handle geometry, fence edges, and the wearer’s silhouette are unreliable because of smoothing, merged regions, and abrupt brightness artifacts.
descriptions.segmentation: The segmentation map consistently isolates one person—the camera wearer—across the lower part of all five frames, with arms extending upward toward the mower handle; no separate person is visible, so facing direction or gaze of another person cannot be established. The wearer occupies the nearest approximately 0.2–0.7 m, but the mower, grass, fence, and building are mostly left unsegmented, preventing dependable object-to-object distances beyond the RGB estimate that the mower is roughly 0.7–1.5 m ahead and within arm’s reach. Across time, the person mask moves and changes orientation from lower-left/centre to lower-right and back, matching body turning, while portions of the head, arms, and torso are clipped by image boundaries or broken by the handle and background. The map clarifies which visible regions belong to the wearer despite self-occlusion, but its occasional “cell phone” label near the hand/handle and fragmented or missing body regions appear unreliable.
descriptions.pose: The pose map detects only sparse magenta hand structures and no dependable yellow body skeleton, locating the wearer’s hands near the upper-middle areas where they contact or approach the mower handle; these hands are roughly 0.5–1.0 m from the camera and within the wearer’s arm span. Their locations shift from near the centre in frame 1 to left-of-centre in frame 2, right-of-centre in frame 3, two separated hand regions in frame 4, and no clear hand detection in frame 5, supporting substantial turning and changing hand visibility. The map makes hand placement and occasional separation clearer than RGB, especially where hands overlap the handle, but it supplies no reliable scene layout, distances between background objects, body orientation, or gaze. Missing joints, isolated fragments, edge-clipped detections, and the disappearance of hands despite their RGB visibility make the pose estimates unreliable for full-body geometry or approach and retreat.
